sections.h2: Selling a Neenah house on your own schedule
sections.html:
Your routes in Neenah: an agent, a do-it-yourself sale, or a cash buyer who takes the house with its flaws. A home ready for move-in and an owner with time suit a listing. A house needing work, an estate or an unmovable closing date suits direct sale.

Neenah counts 27,638 residents, with about 66.2 percent of homes owner-occupied. Owner-occupied homes were valued at a median of $210,700 for 2020 to 2024. Owners with a mortgage typically spend $1,415 a month on housing, and the median household earns $75,374. At 9.37 square miles, Neenah is compact, and the average commute is 18.1 minutes. Buyers who work nearby may value that.

sections.h2: The assessor and your home's record
sections.html:
Questions about assessments belong with the Division of Community Development, 211 Walnut St., Room 313. Appointments are booked at 920-886-6115 or assessors@neenahwi.gov. Staff there look after non-waterfront homes. Waterfront residential and commercial properties belong to a statutory assessor from Associated Appraisal Consultants, Inc., at 920-749-1995.

An appraiser who visits to verify records carries city photo identification and drives a city vehicle. Did a letter from the office arrive while you were getting ready to sell? Book the visit. Correct counts of bedrooms, finished space and additions mean fewer surprises when the buyer's side does its homework. A Department of Revenue guide for owners is linked from the office's page.

On the planning forms page you will find a Tourist House Permit for short-term rentals, a home occupation application and a driveway standards sheet. Guests staying at your house? Check the permit with Community Development before marketing it as a rental, and find out if it passes to a buyer.

A zoning application for site plan review, rezoning and plats is linked from there too. Building permits come from the Inspections division. Call it when earlier work may have gone unpermitted.

Put these in one folder before the first showing.

  • Your tax bill, which shows the parcel identification number the deed needs, and any special assessment figures.
  • Permit records for earlier work. When a past owner finished work with no permit, call the Inspections division.
  • Tourist House Permit paperwork, if guests ever stayed.
  • A corrected assessment record, if the Assessment office wrote to you about the house.
  • The payoff figure from your lender, so you can judge any offer by its net.

Neenah is a lake and river city, roughly 10 miles northeast of Oshkosh. Valley Transit runs buses, I-41 follows the west edge, and flights leave from Appleton International Airport. It is the southwesternmost of the Fox Cities and shares Doty Island with its twin city, Menasha. Waterfront settings draw interest from buyers who use mortgages, so describe yours plainly when you list.

Neenah Joint School District runs one high school and one middle school, with elementary options that include Alliance Charter School and Clayton, Coolidge, Horace Mann, Lakeview, Spring Road, Taft and Tullar elementary schools, plus the Washington School of Early Learning. Look at the boundary map for grades K to 4 to see which elementary school covers a particular address, and mention it when you list.

Properties with one to four units are covered by Wis. Stat. 709.02, which requires you to get a real estate condition report to the buyer within 10 days of acceptance. Fail to, and the buyer may rescind during the next two business days. Leave no item blank, because the report is not complete until every item has an answer or supplied information.

Wis. Stat. 77.22 sets a transfer fee of 30 cents per $100 and makes the seller, as grantor, pay it. The register takes payment together with the deed. A few transfers are exempt.

  • A deed in lieu of foreclosure, or a transfer by will or survivorship, owes no fee.
  • Family transfers for nominal or no consideration, such as parent to child, are exempt under section 77.25. Selling to a relative at a normal price is taxed like any other sale.
  • Whenever the fee is not owed, the deed itself has to state why.

Winnebago County records Neenah deeds, and its Register of Deeds is strict about form.

What a Winnebago County deed needs
RequirementDetail
PartiesGrantor and grantee named
SignatureNotarized grantor signature
PropertyLegal description, plus the parcel identification number from the tax bill under the return address
Return addressShown on the deed
OriginalOriginal deed and original signatures only; no photocopies
Recording fee$30

Bring the Wisconsin transfer return receipt with the deed, plus the recording fee and any transfer fee. The office number is 920-232-3394. Staff give general guidance only. They will not answer legal questions or show you how to fill out the return, so let an attorney or title company draft the deed.

Tax values are fixed on January 1. Bills reach owners by the third Monday in December. Of the two installments, one is due January 31 and the other July 31, and interest of 1 percent per month builds on unpaid tax from February 1.

Special assessments can sit on top of the tax. The City of Neenah or the Winnebago County treasurer can give you the current bill and any such assessments. How the year's tax is split between you and the buyer is the closing agent's job.

A cash offer usually costs some price and buys certainty. Open houses disappear, and so do loan waits and arguments about repairs. Title work sets the closing date. A listing puts the house before the most buyers, and Neenah's lake and river settings attract people who finance.

  • Insist the offer be written, with a closing date and a named payer for title costs.
  • Deduct payoff, unpaid taxes and liens from the price. What remains is your net.
  • Weigh that net against a listing after repairs and carrying costs.

The condition report is your first deadline after accepting an offer. A half-finished report does not count, so answer every item. While you do, ask for the current tax bill and any special assessment figures, and settle with the buyer who will pay for title work.

Next, the deed gets drafted by an attorney or title company from the parcel number on the tax bill. After you file the transfer return, the receipt goes to the Register of Deeds with $30 for recording and any transfer fee owed. Only the original deed, with original signatures, can be recorded.

A cash sale keeps all of these steps. Only the front end differs, since nobody waits on loan underwriting.

faqs.a: Winnebago County. Its Register of Deeds records a deed for $30 and needs the electronic transfer return receipt delivered along with it. The office answers at 920-232-3394.

faqs.q: Who values waterfront homes in Neenah?
faqs.a: A statutory assessor from Associated Appraisal Consultants, Inc. handles residential waterfront and commercial property. Other residential property goes through the city assessment staff at 920-886-6115.

faqs.q: Is a permit needed to rent my Neenah house by the night?
faqs.a: The city lists a Tourist House Permit for short-term rentals on its planning forms page. Ask Community Development if your house already has one and if a buyer could take it over.

faqs.q: Which schools serve a Neenah address?
faqs.a: Neenah Joint School District covers the city. Check the K to 4 boundary map for the elementary school tied to your street.

faqs.q: What is the transfer fee when I sell?
faqs.a: Thirty cents per $100 of value, paid by the seller. A will transfer, a deed in lieu of foreclosure and certain family transfers are exempt.
